title: Orthogonal cache-key design + TTL annealing playbook for safe cost reduction
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: We need a reproducible, low-risk playbook to reduce per-token cost using smarter KV/prefix caching: combine orthogonal cache-key design, hit-rate curve modeling, and progressive TTL annealing with automated safety gates and deterministic rollback. This ticket captures modeling approach, config heuristics, canary strategy, metrics and automation required to safely apply and revert cache changes for both Hosted API and Dedicated pools.

Problem: Current prefix caching yields uneven hit-rate uplift; naive longer TTLs reduce token cost but increase stale responses and memory pressure. Cache key granularity varies across services, causing both over-splitting (low hit rate) and over-aggregation (incorrect reuse). We lack a single playbook to: 1) predict hit-rate and cost impact from proposed key/TTL changes, 2) apply changes with observable safety gates, and 3) rollback automatically or manually when regression occurs.

Goals:
- Produce a modeling harness that estimates token savings and memory delta from key/TTL changes using historical trace replay.
- Provide a set of heuristics for cache-key orthogonality (what attributes to include/exclude) to maximize effective reuse while avoiding correctness issues.
- Define safe TTL annealing policy with canary gradients, automated rollback triggers, and post-apply monitoring dashboards.
- Implement an automation script/CI job to run preflight simulations and generate human-readable recommendations for SRE/Platform owners.
acceptance_criteria: Modeling harness can run on 30-day traces and produce per-prefix predicted hit-rate and token-savings CSV
A 3-stage TTL annealing plan (canary 1%, ramp 10%, ramp 50%/100%) documented with success thresholds
Automated rollback triggers implemented: hit-rate drop > 2% absolute for critical prefixes OR latency increase > 15th percentile SLA
Cache-key canonicalization ruleset (.md) with examples for 6 product surfaces (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank)
Playbook changes reviewed by PM and Design for customer-impact scenarios and signed off
tasks: Build trace replay adapter that simulates cache hits for proposed key/TTL configs (owner: Marcus)
Implement hit-curve fitter that outputs hit-rate vs TTL per prefix (owner: Data Eng)
Draft canonicalization ruleset and example transformations for keys (owner: Platform)
Create observability dashboard: per-prefix hit-rate, memory footprint, per-token cost, and latency quantiles (owner: Observability)
Add canary rollout script with automated rollback conditions to infra-automation repo (owner: SRE)
Run pilot on two low-risk prefixes and prepare incident-free runbook (owner: Marcus)
Document final playbook in Confluence with links to simulation CSVs and PRs (owner: Aisha)
metrics: Observed cache hit-rate delta (absolute) after apply
Per-token cost reduction (USD/token) and estimated monthly savings
95th latency quantile before and after change
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggregation causes cross-customer leakage or stale outputs. Mitigation: conservative canonicalization, strip only non-deterministic attributes, add tenant-scope to keys for multi-tenant surfaces.
Risk: Memory pressure on Dedicated pools. Mitigation: enforce per-pool memory thresholds and LB-based eviction policy; simulate memory delta before apply.
Risk: False positive hit-rate improvements due to test-time caching. Mitigation: use shadow-mode replay and off-line simulation rather than live sampling for initial estimate.
Risk: Automation rollback flapping. Mitigation: require 3 consecutive evaluation windows before auto-rollback and add manual confirmation gate for high-impact prefixes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Preflight simulation on 30-day traces + PR with recommended key changes and TTL. Phase 1 (Canary): apply policy to 1% of traffic for 24h with strict auto-rollback thresholds. Phase 2 (Ramp): if stable, expand to 10% for 48h, then 50% for 72h. Phase 3 (Full): 100% with continued monitoring and 7-day observation window. Each phase must meet thresholds for hit-rate uplift, no latency regressions, and memory under configurable thresholds.
